claim: Workflow mutable state updates, durable history event appends, and asynchronous execution task generation (transfer, timer, visibility, replication) are committed in a single atomic persistence transaction guarded by the shard RangeID.
mechanism: The history engine executes mutations through TransactionImpl.UpdateWorkflowExecution. In closeTransactionPrepareTasks, pending task definitions are converted into execution tasks and serialized into the same persistence request as the mutable state mutation and history event batch.
applicabilityConditions: All active workflow execution state transitions (activity scheduled, timer started, workflow completion, signal handling, child workflow spawn)
Both SQL and NoSQL persistence implementations adhering to Temporal execution manager contracts

Known limits: Speculative workflow tasks (used for synchronous update/query evaluation) deliberately bypass persistence and do not generate transactional tasks until committed. Task generation assumes the database transaction provides atomic all-or-nothing guarantees across mutable state and outbox tables.

sourceProvenance.queryOrCodeSnippet: Persists history events, updates workflow mutable state mutation, and generates transactional outbox tasks (transfer, timer, visibility) in a single transactional database call guarded by the shard RangeID.

claim: History shards enforce mutual exclusion and fence zombie hosts using a monotonically increasing persistent RangeID. Any persistence write attempted by a host with an outdated RangeID fails immediately, triggering engine shutdown.
mechanism: Shard context maintains a lease RangeID. All execution updates pass the current RangeID. When persistence detects a RangeID mismatch or ShardOwnershipLostError, handleWriteErrorLocked triggers a contextRequestStop transition, terminating the history engine and clearing in-memory cached workflow states.
applicabilityConditions: History service shard lifecycle management during node restarts, cluster rebalancing, network partitions, and host crashes
localContext: Shard context maintains a lease RangeID. All execution updates pass the current RangeID. When persistence detects a RangeID mismatch or ShardOwnershipLostError, handleWriteErrorLocked triggers a contextRequestStop transition, terminating the history engine and clearing in-memory cached workflow states. Known limits: In-flight uncommitted memory computations prior to persistence write attempts are discarded, relying on idempotency of client retries. Requires database supporting atomic conditional updates on shard records (e.g. Cassandra lightweight transactions or SQL row locks).

sourceProvenance.queryOrCodeSnippet: Validates incoming write request RangeID against the shard lease RangeID. If ShardOwnershipLostError is returned from persistence, triggers an immediate shard transition to stop engine execution to prevent split-brain state mutations.

claim: Failed or timed-out workflow tasks on attempt > 1 do not append failure events to persistent history. Instead, retry attempts are tracked ephemerally in mutable state as transient workflow tasks, preventing history bloat under poison workloads.
mechanism: When a workflow task fails or times out, ApplyTransientWorkflowTaskScheduled increments the attempt count in mutable state but suppresses writing WorkflowTaskScheduled and WorkflowTaskStarted events to history. Only upon final successful task completion are the started and completed events appended.
applicabilityConditions: Workflow task execution failures caused by worker crashes, transient bugs, network timeouts, or non-deterministic code changes on retry
localContext: When a workflow task fails or times out, ApplyTransientWorkflowTaskScheduled increments the attempt count in mutable state but suppresses writing WorkflowTaskScheduled and WorkflowTaskStarted events to history. Only upon final successful task completion are the started and completed events appended. Known limits: If a failover happens while a transient task is scheduled, the standby cluster reconciles the attempt counter and converts the task back to a standard scheduled task. Permanent workflow code bugs will retry indefinitely (unless WorkflowTaskScheduleToStart/Close timeouts or max attempts are configured).

sourceProvenance.queryOrCodeSnippet: When a workflow task fails or times out (attempt > 1), creates an in-memory transient workflow task without persisting WorkflowTaskScheduled or WorkflowTaskStarted events to durable history, preserving history determinism and bounding event growth.

mechanism: MutableStateImpl diverts new events to bufferEventsInDB while a workflow task is in Started status. In closeTransactionPrepareEvents, buffered events are flushed into history only after the running task completes or times out, triggering a subsequent workflow task if necessary.
applicabilityConditions: Concurrent signals, external cancellation requests, child workflow completions, and activity completions arriving during active workflow task execution
localContext: MutableStateImpl diverts new events to bufferEventsInDB while a workflow task is in Started status. Known limits: Buffered events are committed in batch after workflow task completion, creating discrete state transition boundaries. Excessive buffered events are bounded by mutable state size checks to prevent memory exhaustion.

sourceProvenance.queryOrCodeSnippet: External events arriving while a workflow task is in Started status on a worker are diverted to buffered events in mutable state, ensuring the running worker executes against a consistent history snapshot without race conditions.

claim: The Matching service achieves sub-millisecond task dispatch latency by matching producer push with long-polling worker pull over unbuffered Go channels (taskC), spilling to persistent task queue tables only when pollers are absent.
mechanism: TaskMatcher.Offer attempts synchronous hand-off to waiting pollers on taskC. If no poller receives the task within the configured timeout or if rate limits apply, the task is committed to the database backlog via taskWriter and loaded by taskReader as pollers arrive.
applicabilityConditions: Workflow task and activity task dispatch in the Matching service under normal and overloaded operating conditions
localContext: TaskMatcher.Offer attempts synchronous hand-off to waiting pollers on taskC. If no poller receives the task within the configured timeout or if rate limits apply, the task is committed to the database backlog via taskWriter and loaded by taskReader as pollers arrive. Known limits: When no pollers are connected for a queue, all tasks incur persistence round-trips. Requires partitioned task queues to scale poller throughput across multiple matching hosts.

claim: During active-passive multi-cluster failover with divergent history branches, Temporal identifies the last common ancestor using version history trees, rebuilds mutable state to the winning branch, and automatically salvages and reapplies orphaned external signals.
mechanism: ConflictResolver uses version history comparison to find branch fork points. StateRebuilder reconstructs mutable state from history events up to the fork point. EventsReapplier iterates over events on the abandoned branch and re-injects signals and external updates into the new active branch.
applicabilityConditions: Multi-cluster active-passive replication topologies during disaster recovery failovers, network splits, and namespace active cluster migrations
localContext: ConflictResolver uses version history comparison to find branch fork points. StateRebuilder reconstructs mutable state from history events up to the fork point. EventsReapplier iterates over events on the abandoned branch and re-injects signals and external updates into the new active branch. Known limits: Only external signals and idempotent updates can be safely reapplied; non-idempotent side effects executed in external systems must be handled by application-level sagas. Workflows that closed on an orphaned branch cannot have closed statuses overturned without explicit admin reset.

sourceProvenance.queryOrCodeSnippet: When active-passive cluster failover causes history branch divergence, reapplies uncommitted external signals and events from the abandoned branch onto the new active branch to prevent signal loss across failover boundaries.

mechanism: timerSequenceImpl evaluates four deadline points (schedule-to-close, schedule-to-start, start-to-close, heartbeat) before and after state transitions and computes a changedMask. Timer status bits are cleared and tasks recreated only for deadlines whose actual timestamp changed.
applicabilityConditions: Activity retry scheduling, long-running activities with schedule-to-close timeouts, and passive cluster replication loops
localContext: timerSequenceImpl evaluates four deadline points (schedule-to-close, schedule-to-start, start-to-close, heartbeat) before and after state transitions and computes a changedMask. sourceProvenance.queryOrCodeSnippet: Activity timer regeneration compares schedule-to-close, schedule-to-start, start-to-close, and heartbeat deadlines before and after state transitions, preserving active timer status bits when deadlines remain unchanged to avoid timer task storms.

claim: Synchronous workflow updates provide atomic request-validation-execution semantics where validation failures are rejected in worker memory without polluting persistent history, while accepted updates commit durable progress.
mechanism: Update registry coordinates a two-phase protocol: Phase 1 dispatches a validation invocation to the SDK worker; if validation fails, an error is returned synchronously to the caller with zero history events generated. Phase 2 generates WorkflowExecutionUpdateAccepted event upon validation success.
applicabilityConditions: Synchronous query-and-mutate workflows, financial balance checks, atomic approvals, and interactive workflow modifications
localContext: Update registry coordinates a two-phase protocol: Phase 1 dispatches a validation invocation to the SDK worker; if validation fails, an error is returned synchronously to the caller with zero history events generated. Phase 2 generates WorkflowExecutionUpdateAccepted event upon validation success. Known limits: Requires worker support for update handlers and speculative execution protocol. Speculative update tasks must be cleared from memory if the workflow execution is evicted or evicted before completion.

claim: Reading mutable state fields after invoking the workflow lease release function creates high-concurrency data races with incoming signals or updates; mutable state data must be copied by value before releasing the execution semaphore.
mechanism: Workflow execution locks protect mutable state integrity. In UpdateWithStart (Invoke), reading ExecutionState.Status after workflowLease.GetReleaseFn()(nil) allowed concurrent writers to race on the status field. The fix captures status into a stack-allocated variable before releasing the lock.

claim: Parent close policies (TERMINATE, ABANDON, REQUEST_CANCEL) for child workflows are decoupled from parent workflow completion transactions via asynchronous transfer tasks, guaranteeing parent close latency is bounded regardless of child hierarchy depth.
mechanism: When a parent workflow closes, GenerateWorkflowCloseTasks writes parent close policy records into child workflow transfer tasks. Dedicated worker queue processors (service/worker/parentclosepolicy) consume the tasks and execute cancellation/termination RPCs asynchronously.
applicabilityConditions: Parent workflows orchestrating child workflows across multiple namespaces, clusters, or execution partitions
localContext: When a parent workflow closes, GenerateWorkflowCloseTasks writes parent close policy records into child workflow transfer tasks. Dedicated worker queue processors (service/worker/parentclosepolicy) consume the tasks and execute cancellation/termination RPCs asynchronously. Known limits: ABANDON policy requires no action and produces no transfer task. Under extreme system worker backlog, child termination may lag behind parent close by queue processing latency.
